key_points: A Delhi court acquitted former WFI chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh of sexual harassment charges in August.
A Goa Bench convicted Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal and criticized the trial court for relying on victim stereotypes.
Senior Advocate Rebecca John stated the Delhi judgment misread evidence and unfairly doubted the complainants.
The Goa Bench ruled that credibility must be evaluated on facts rather than a narrow cultural mould of ideal victim behavior.
items.summary: Two Indian courts delivered contrasting judgments in August regarding sexual harassment cases against influential men. A Delhi court acquitted former Wrestling Federation of India chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, while a Goa Bench convicted Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal. The Delhi court acquitted Singh based on the complainants' conduct and lack of immediate complaints, raising concerns about victim stereotypes. Conversely, the Goa Bench convicted Tejpal and criticized the trial court for relying on the 'perfect victim' myth and invasive cross-examination. Senior Advocate Rebecca John argued the Delhi judgment misread evidence and favored the accused, while the Goa order marked a departure from cultural archetypes regarding trauma. Both judgments highlight the tension between judicial standards of proof and societal expectations of survivor behavior. The Supreme Court is now reviewing Tejpal's appeal, and both cases may be appealed further.
items.title: Two courts rule differently on sexual harassment cases involving powerful men

key_points: China deleted flood videos and restricted foreign journalist access to the Tibet disaster zone.
State media emphasized rescue operations and leadership visits while omitting local community impacts.
Professor Wanning Sun compares current restrictions to previous controlled coverage of the 2008 Sichuan earthquake.
The information gap between restricted Chinese reporting and Western access fuels mutual distrust.
Laura Bicker reported that Beijing fears instability in the politically sensitive Tibet region.
items.summary: The article reports that China is tightly controlling the narrative surrounding recent floods in Tibet by deleting videos and censoring news. Laura Bicker of the BBC noted that footage of the Gyirong Port disaster was scrubbed from platforms like Weixin and RedNote due to fears of instability. Allyson Horn of the Australian Broadcasting Corporation stated she was denied access to Tibet despite repeated requests, alongside other foreign journalists blocked from the region. State media coverage focuses on rescue operations and leadership visits while avoiding reports on local villagers' suffering. Professor Wanning Sun explains that this approach follows a pattern of restricted coverage seen in past disasters like the 2008 Sichuan earthquake and the 2011 Wenzhou train accident. The resulting information gap fuels Western suspicions of bias while reinforcing Beijing's belief that external reporting is inherently hostile.
items.title: China restricts Tibet flood reporting while state media emphasizes positive narratives

key_points: Sayandeb Chowdhury's new book analyzes the life and enduring cultural impact of Uttam Kumar in Bengali cinema.

items.summary: Sayandeb Chowdhury explores the life and cultural impact of Uttam Kumar in a new book titled *Uttam Kumar, A Life in Cinema*. The author reports that Kumar dominated Bengali cinema between the early 1950s and late 1970s, commanding both commercial success and cultural reverence. Chowdhury writes that Kumar's star persona remains undiminished four decades after his 1980 death, with his films continuing to attract regular audiences. The text notes that Kumar transitioned from a cashier to a celebrated actor, achieving stardom with hits like *Bosu Poribar* and *Sharey Chuattor*. The author states that Kumar founded an actors' union and advocated for industry development while receiving numerous awards. Chowdhury argues that Kumar's influence extends beyond cinema, serving as a central figure in post-Tagorean Bengali public life. The book, set for publication in 2026, aims to analyze the unique nature of Kumar's stardom and his lasting mythos.
items.title: Author examines Uttam Kumar's enduring legacy in Bengali cinema

items.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu released Godavari waters to North Andhra through the Polavaram Project Left Main Canal on Wednesday. The Rs 4,192-crore canal, spanning 213 km, will initially irrigate 2.87 lakh acres and provide drinking water to 5.23 lakh people. Naidu stated the project would help North Andhra emerge as a major development hub. He announced plans to complete 12 major projects costing Rs 3,200 crore and assured that 36 projects worth Rs 35,000 crore would be finished in three years. Naidu also criticized the previous YSRCP government for alleged mismanagement of funds and accused them of spreading false propaganda regarding data centres. He highlighted cooperation with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to strengthen key state initiatives.
items.title: CM Naidu releases Godavari waters to North Andhra via Polavaram canal

key_points: Dr Subhash Chandra's lawyers told the NCLAT that media coverage caused unfair reputational damage regarding a Rs 6.5 crore repayment proposal.

items.summary: ACE Equity data shows nine Indian midcap stocks became multibaggers over two years while the broader Nifty 50 slipped. Laurus Labs led gains at 296%, followed by BSE at 243% and Multi Commodity Exchange at 219%. Other top performers included Hitachi Energy India, One97 Communications, GE Vernova T&D India, Lloyds Metals & Energy, Radico Khaitan, and National Aluminium Company.
